A hollowed nickel-iron asteroid in orbit of the gas giant Nhai, spun for gravity, eleven kilometres long. Built by the Halden-Ash Company as the Sabra Concern's habitat. Lit from within by the Wick.
The fusion lamp that runs down Lantern's axis like a candle-wick: the habitat's sun. Tended from catwalks and crawls along the spine. Fed by fuel cassettes.
The terraced housing rings carved into Lantern's inner wall, where the indentured live: bunk-rooms, chit-shops, pump galleries.
Lantern's docking ring at the fore end of the rock, where the haulers come in from Caul. The Ardent Mercy's bell hangs at the inner lock, on the Bell Hook.
The vault at Lantern's core where the Tally engine runs, with the Company's offices above it. In the Owing it is the seat of the Count, built over the Hulk.
Lantern's air plant and water stills, deep in the fore wall. Every scrubber and valve is keyed to the Tally.
The best-lit terraces near Lantern's fore end, nearest the Counting House. Company staff housing in 2387; the counting families' quarter in the Owing.
Lantern's aft sections, abandoned, unheated and unlit: frozen streets, frost on the walls, and the dead of earlier centuries. Cutters strip them for metal.
A ship-shaped mass embedded in the rock under the Counting House since the Closing. The Owing believe it is the Ardent Mercy, the ship that brought the first families.
The old ice docks at the aft end of the Dock Ring, half-abandoned, where the Salt land ice run off Caul outside the Tally.
Nhai's ice moon. Lantern's water comes from it.
The Company's deep ice mine on Caul. Shut down in the spring of 2387.
The wormhole at the edge of the Sabra system, Lantern's only road to the Concord.
The gas giant Lantern orbits. Banded ochre and bruise-purple, with a thin ring.
The Halden-Ash Company's last ship in the Sabra system, a long-haul carrier docked at Lantern's fore lock.
Kas Ostrova's ice hauler: a battered tug with a tank-frame, on the Caul run.
The Company's monitoring station near the Throat, which measures the wormhole's breathing.
Concord frontier station on the far side of the Throat, built when the Throat was dead, waiting seven hundred years for it to heal.
A Throat-runner ship out of Port Ambry, mortgaged to Brightwater Recovery, captained by Mabry Ode.
